extracted.intended_audience: founders, startup marketers, and PR people at early-stage companies
extracted.subtask_description: Practical how-to guidance for startups on finding, building relationships with, and pitching journalists to earn media coverage. Focuses on sourcing contacts, crafting pitches, using assets, and selecting angles that appeal to reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target journalists who are most likely going to be interested in your story
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the most important part. No matter how well worded your pitch is, if you’re pitching a tech product to a fashion journalist, it’s going to fall flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search Google News using a few general keywords related to your company, click through to recent articles (past ~3 weeks), and find the journalist’s bio (often with a link to their Twitter) to learn what they cover. Add every relevant journalist you discover who covers topics related to your company. Avoid pitching irrelevant beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a structured journalist spreadsheet (required columns)
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep all the relevant journalists you find in one place, create a spreadsheet with the following columns:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns to include: Full name of the journalist; Email address of the journalist; Link to the article you discovered them on; Link to the Twitter profile of the journalist; Timezone of the journalist (based on the city they live in) - this is so you can send your pitch when they are most likely working/checking their emails. Use this sheet to aggregate and track outreach. The timezone column is explicitly to time your outreach when journalists are likely checking email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and validate journalist email addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: To get each journalist’s email address, enter the URL of the publication they write for into emailhunter.co. It’ll return the emails of some of the people who work there and let you infer the publication’s formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: entering Forbes into Email Hunter can reveal a pattern like firstinitiallastname@forbes.com so you can guess a journalist’s likely address (e.g., Sam Harris -> sharris@forbes.com). The article also recommends using JustReachOut to automatically provide the most recent validated email addresses and to report invalid addresses so they can be updated within 24 hours. Validate emails where possible and track validation status in your spreadsheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build relationships with journalists first (don’t cold-blast unsolicited pitches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are much more likely to at least give your pitch a chance if you built a relationship with them beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participate in online discussions of topics related to your company (e.g., Quora), leave meaningful comments, and then reach out asking for the journalist’s expertise (sample outreach provided). Example template: “Hey Journalist, I noticed you’ve been writing about the SEO skyscraper technique a lot lately, I just answered a question on Quora... I’m writing a blog post on this topic and would love to feature your answer in my blog post. Feel free to comment directly on the thread. Thank you a bunch ahead of time! -Dmitry” The post advises starting PR outreach before your company officially launches and warns that emailing out of the blue with unsolicited advice “doesn’t quite work.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer interesting visual content assets with your pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of just offering a text-only pitch, use visual assets to instantly explain what your company does and why it matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: visuals are processed much faster than text (post claims 60,000x faster). Examples: infographics (e.g., how a Tesla works), annotated app screenshots or onboarding screens to show main features. The less time it takes a journalist to understand what you do, the less likely your pitch will be skipped or forgotten.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find journalists who are actively looking for sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Target journalists who are already requesting companies and people to feature in stories they’re currently working on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods: sign up for HARO (they send journalist queries twice daily); skim each day’s email for relevant requests and reply to queries that match your expertise; search Twitter for #journorequest plus keywords; use JustReachOut to pull real-time journalist queries from multiple sources and reply directly inside the platform. Pitching in response to an active query increases the chance of being included since the reporter is already working on the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start by pitching local publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Local publications can be much easier to break into early on because starting a company in a city can be newsworthy locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a list of every local publication in your city and find a journalist at each whose beat is relevant. Include college alumni publications. Use local coverage as credibility to move up to larger outlets. The post includes a local pitch template that offers an exclusive coupon or first-delivery free to entice coverage, and suggests tailoring the pitch to the publication’s audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch a compelling angle related to your company (don’t only pitch the product)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless your company is truly world-changing, the mere news of its launch is rarely enough; pitch a compelling angle because journalists write about larger issues and movements and mention companies relevant to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested angles include: The personal angle (your background and journey — humanizes the story and can be used in larger issue pieces; sample template and Tristan Walker example provided), The interesting context angle (position your company as an example in a broader trend or movement — Forbes peer-to-peer sharing economy example; Soylent example). The post gives templates for each angle and emphasizes that these angles make your story more emotionally and contextually engaging for journalists' audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and analyze interesting data that aligns with a journalist’s beat
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract interesting behavior patterns or other data-driven findings from your product and turn them into visualizations and narratives journalists will find newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish findings on your blog with snazzy charts, promote them in relevant online communities so journalists can discover them, or proactively pitch journalists with the data. Example: OkCupid used aggregated dating behavior patterns and shared highlights (e.g., racial bias patterns) as hooky story material. The post provides a template pitch for data-driven stories that lists highlights and suggests questions journalists might explore, plus an attached overview of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use short, personalized pitch templates and tactical incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concise, personalized messages tailored to the journalist and the chosen angle; consider offering exclusives or incentives to make the pitch more appealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the post include multiple sample pitch texts (local pitch offering an exclusive coupon, personal-angle pitch describing founder struggles, context-angle pitch connecting product to a broader trend). The guidance implies avoiding long walls of text, being relevant to the journalist’s beat, offering helpful assets (images, data, exclusives), and asking a clear question like “Is this a good fit for your audience?” Use signed, human signoffs and keep pitches conversational and respectful of journalists’ time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tools and automation to scale sourcing and outreach (but maintain quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automate journalist discovery, email guessing, query scraping, and contact management to scale outreach while preserving relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JustReachOut’s workflow: enter general keywords, the system finds recent related articles and allows adding journalists to your pitch list with a + button; it returns validated email addresses and supports reporting bad addresses for correction within 24 hours. The post recommends automating discovery (e.g., pulling #journorequest or HARO queries) but emphasizes that targeting and relationship-building must remain intentional to avoid generic, irrelevant pitches.
